Interview with Lawrence Brown
by Patricia Willard
Reel Five

PRO-TYPISTS, INC.
PROFESSIONAL TRANSCRIPTION SERVICE
AREA CODE 202 347-5395
You were saying that Juan Tizol wrote prettier, right?
Yes, he did, uh-huh. I knew he did cause I had to sit next to him for weeks and weeks in the theaters -- dressing rooms. And he kept drilling at this tune he had in his mind, which was "Perdido."
you said he was what -- singing it?
Humming it to his self -- you know. Getting the melody together.
Did he write any other? The only two I'm aware of are "Caravan" and "Perdido" "Beyha." (PHONETIC)

He has a real pretty tune called "Lost In Meditation" and he wrote -- altogether I think he has about seven tunes. But outside of those first three, I don't think the others have been exploited very much.
You mentioned that until he wrote "Caravan" well he never played solos much. Is that what you were saying?

Before writing "Caravan" he never attempted -- he seemed shy. And he never attempted to play melodies or -- no solos. He never -- I don't think he -- I don't think he ever played a solo except the theme line of "Caravan" and "Perdido" and things like that.
"Lost In Meditation," he played that too. But I don't know -- "Caravan" was just a part of him.
